svg.title: DDIA 2 · DATA MODELS & QUERY LANGUAGES: sketchnote
svg.text: The shape of your data decides which database fits. Trees of data that are read together (one-to-many) suit documents.
Document: a profile is a self-contained tree. One read fetches
it all because the data has locality. This works when the data
is one-to-many and read as a whole.
App code now does the JOIN
Document databases have weak join support, so the join moves
into application code. As data gains references, the relational
There is always a schema, it's just implicit in the reading
code. You still pay for migrations, just later and in more
Query: people born in the US who live in Europe → follow WITHIN* edges, any depth
A recursive query ("WITHIN, any number of hops") is one line in
Cypher and painful in SQL (recursive CTE).
Huge write volume, simple key access
"I start from access patterns. The two hot queries are X and Y, and both are key lookups with one
join, so Postgres with the right indexes covers it. I'd only move to Cassandra if write volume passes
Study notes on Designing Data-Intensive Applications (Kleppmann). Read the book.
